# 2. Approved schematic and system plan

Attach or draw a readable schematic/system diagram. Label:

- source voltage and ground/reference;
- protection and current limiting;
- inputs and sensors;
- controller and exact verified GPIO/ADC connections;
- transistor/MOSFET/driver and flyback protection where required;
- output/load and its separate supply where required;
- component reference designators and values;
- voltage test points; and
- current paths or KCL nodes needed for the analysis.

Use the separate **TEJ Capstone Circuit Reference Diagrams** for layout patterns. Do not copy a reference circuit without adapting it to the verified board, exact parts, ratings, and approved project requirements.

## Measurement-quality check

- [ ] Meter mode, range, and jacks were checked before connection.
- [ ] Voltage was measured across two named points.
- [ ] Resistance/continuity was used only with power removed and stored energy discharged.
- [ ] Values include units and reasonable precision.
- [ ] Unexpected signs, zeros, overloads, or unstable readings were investigated.
- [ ] A photograph/screenshot is approved and does not expose private information.

## Portfolio transfer checklist

- [ ] Problem, user, constraints, and success criteria are clear.
- [ ] Final schematic/system diagram is readable and matches the tested version.
- [ ] Calculations show units, assumptions, and a check.
- [ ] Predicted, simulated, and measured evidence are distinguished.
- [ ] Linux/Python evidence includes meaningful tests, not only a code screenshot.
- [ ] One fault, diagnostic sequence, correction, and retest are explained.
- [ ] Revision and limitations are honest.
- [ ] Images have useful captions and alt text.
- [ ] Sources, collaborators, and adapted material are credited.
- [ ] Student numbers, private accounts, schedules, classroom codes, device identifiers, passwords, tokens, and information about other students are removed.
- [ ] All links work in the rendered portfolio.
